correctness.rationale: Three-periodic weight solution exactly satisfies the recurrence; factorization into \(q^{k(n-k)}\) and residue-count factors is an algebraic identity. Multiples of three have nonnegative count difference; the residue-two count deficit is at most one and occurs only when \(k\ge2\) and \(n-k\ge2\), giving an available \(q^4\) factor. \({4\brack2}_f\) implies \(t\mid q^4\); the divisor pair \((2,4)\) implies \(t\mid q^2\), and a complete residue-class argument proves sufficiency. Finite checker corroborates 1950 parameter pairs but is not used as an infinite proof.
